Prosper just approved a 2 billion dollar Italian village at the Dallas North Tollway and 380.

On October 27, the Prosper Town Council unanimously approved zoning for The Marco, a $2 billion, 143-acre village at the northeast corner of the Dallas North Tollway and US 380. The plan centers on a lagoon of more than 15 acres with canals big enough for boats.

It allows up to 4,400 homes and apartments, office buildings up to 14 stories and up to two hotels. It still needs agreements on incentives, impact fees and open space, and the developer says construction could start by the end of 2026. Nearby Star Trail's typical sale over the last 12 months was $925,000.

Would you want to live next to it?

Every single family rental home now has to register within the City of Allen. Notices came out in November and the deadline is the end of January.

Prosper just approved 10 million dollars to help widen roads, specifically the access roads along the Dallas North Tollway, in early 2027.

On October 27, the Prosper Town Council approved a $10 million contract with Mario Sinacola & Sons, the company building the Dallas North Tollway extension. About $7.2 million repairs the northbound Dallas Parkway frontage road near First Street, Prosper Trail and Frontier Parkway, and $2.8 million widens Frontier Parkway west of Dallas Parkway to match the tollway's wider underpass.

Work is set to start in late January or early February 2027 and run about 120 days. The town hasn't decided whether to close Dallas Parkway in stages or all at once. NTTA says the tollway from US 380 to FM 428 opens in late 2027. Star Trail's typical sale over the last 12 months was $925,000.

McKinney's 334 million dollar Sunset Amphitheater off of 121 and 75 just passed 70 percent complete, and the budget increased by over 100 million.

The Sunset Amphitheater near the northeast corner of US 75 and SH 121 in McKinney is 70 to 75 percent built, per Venu on October 30. It seats up to 20,000, could host up to 100 shows a year, and Venu is targeting completion in the first quarter of 2027. No opening date is set yet.

Venu's cost grew from $220 million to about $334 million. On October 21 it closed a $60 million sale-leaseback of the land with Store Capital to finish construction, after McKinney approved an updated incentive agreement on October 5. The typical McKinney home sold for $500,000 over the last 12 months.
